title: Dual-sphere exchange media
scope: Qualitative dual-sphere exchange pattern for the ridge-spur settlement and the outlet settlement: a prestige coin sphere above an internal customary obligation sphere with socially marked conversion; prices, denominations, rates, quantities, metals, names, scripts, mints, treasuries, markets, harvest-trade practice, compact finance, occurred trade events, and all natural System behaviour remain open or unchanged.
approval_evidence: On 2026-08-17 the Author selected 'Option C — DUAL-SPHERE' from the displayed multiple-choice options, accepting Option C exactly as drafted together with the proposal's shared claim set.
question: Which qualitative pattern governs how value moves in and between the ridge-spur settlement and the outlet settlement — the money-object classes in use, the local credit customs beside them, and how exchange settles under the standing rivalry — without choosing any coin name, denomination, legend, or specific metal; any price, exchange rate, quantity, or unit; any market, assay, mint, toll, tariff, treaty, or trade-good list; any harvest-trade practice or law; any tax, tribute, or compact-finance institution; or any script, literacy claim, or word for money?
selection: Use Option C — DUAL-SPHERE, plus the proposal's shared claim set. Two customary spheres of worth ride one above the other: an external or prestige sphere running on surviving imperial coin — inter-settlement trade, storage of worth, prestige transfers, and, where a consented communal burden is discharged in movable worth at all, the customary medium of that discharge, with no levy, rate, treasury, or compact-finance institution established — and an internal or customary sphere running on obligation, witnessed debts, labour-exchange, tally customs, and in-kind return inside each settlement. Converting between spheres is socially marked — noticed, storied, sometimes resented — with no rule, prohibition, or rate. WLD-EVENT-001's contested-exchange-terms pressure lives in the coin sphere as argument classes over acceptance, wear, and standing: tendencies, never occurred incidents. Each of the three cultures holds a distinct live relationship to the same thinning coin stock — original households keeping to stores, stock, and obligation and using coin as a boundary tool for strangers; imperial-remnant tradition treating coin as a bearer of record and standing; the hybrid braid negotiating two-sphere fluency — each a tendency with internal variation and no unanimity. Salvage coin flows as dispersed single or small finds within WLD-LOCATION-004's salvage activity class, whether the outlet settlement ever tests, re-melts, or strikes metal stays an explicit open question, and coin worth is social belief and custom that the System neither recognises nor attests.
alternatives: Option A — DEAD-STANDARD COINS: old imperial coin in qualitative higher-worth and lower-worth metal classes remains the region's one trusted movable medium, trusted on metal content and long familiarity and on no surviving authority, with tally-and-trust credit carrying daily exchange inside each settlement and coin reserved for storage, once-off transfers, and dealings between strangers. Not selected.

Option B — WEIGHED-METAL AND TALLY: coin faith broke with the empire, the money-object classes are weighed metal in qualitative worth classes and workable metal stock, old coins persist as bullion or keepsakes, notched-tally credit carries daily life, and the outlet settlement's metal capability makes it the natural supplier and validator of weighed metal. Not selected.

Option C — DUAL-SPHERE: an external or prestige sphere of surviving imperial coin rides above an internal or customary sphere of obligation, labour-exchange, tallies, and in-kind return; conversion between spheres is socially marked; the rivalry's contested exchange terms live in the coin sphere; and each of the three cultures holds a distinct live relationship to the same coin stock. Selected.
rationale: The selected pattern lets the trade rivalry and settlement politics both speak through money without inventing a single institution, gives each of the three cultures a distinct, live relationship to the same coin stock rather than a shared attitude, and keeps minting and validation open as a future story lever for the outlet settlement's metal advantage.
evidence: Author selection on 2026-08-17: 'Option C — DUAL-SPHERE' chosen from the displayed multiple-choice options, with the proposal's shared claim set.
consequences: Two customary spheres of worth exist: an external or prestige sphere of surviving imperial coin — inter-settlement trade, storage of worth, prestige transfers, and the customary medium where a consented communal burden is discharged in movable worth at all — and an internal or customary sphere of obligation, witnessed debts, labour-exchange, tally customs, and in-kind return.

Imperial coin circulates in qualitative worth classes sourced from pre-drawdown holdings, salvage finds, and cross-lake inflow; no authority mints or validates coin; wear, clipping, and hoarding attrition are live qualitative concerns and the trusted stock is thinning.
No functioning imperial mint or treasury authority survives anywhere in the region, and no community currently mints coin.

Internal-sphere credit customs are qualitative only — witnessed debts, obligation held in memory and in tally media, labour-exchange, and in-kind return — with no ledger institution, unit, record form, office, or enforcement established.
Conversion between spheres is socially marked — noticed, storied, sometimes resented — with no rule, prohibition, or rate, and the marking itself varies by household and situation.

WLD-EVENT-001's contested-exchange-terms pressure expresses itself in the external sphere as argument classes over coin acceptance, wear, and standing; these are tendencies, and no occurred exchange, negotiation, embargo, or incident is established.

Coin-facing tendencies hold with internal variation and no unanimity: original-culture households keep to the internal sphere of stores, stock, and obligation and use coin as a boundary tool for strangers; imperial-remnant tradition treats coin as a bearer of record and standing; the hybrid braid negotiates two-sphere fluency, with straddling households often brokering conversions. These are attitudes toward money objects and exchange media only.
The outlet settlement tends to treat the coin sphere as native ground; the hillfort tends to treat it as an instrument for dealing outward.

Salvage coin from remnant ground is dispersed single or small finds within WLD-LOCATION-004's salvage activity class — finite, diminishing, contestable, with no right, ownership, law, market, or price — and that record's no-cache default stands, so no coin hoard exists by implication.
Whether the outlet settlement ever tests, re-melts, or strikes metal or coin is an explicit open question; no mint, assay, or validation institution exists.
Coin worth is social belief and custom; the System recognises no currency, attests no value, and no readout, Skill, appraisal, or office guarantees a coin's or metal's worth.

Declared bounded closure of part of WLD-LOCATION-005's open economy-and-institution space and its open-other-communities boundary: no community in the region currently mints coin or holds treasury authority; everything else those openings hold stays open.
WLD-ECOLOGY-006's harvest-institution boundary and WLD-CULTURE-002's open compact-finance space stay untouched, and no harvest share is a money object.

The Author-directed founding frame is established by canon://world/shared-universe-001/culture/settlement-founding-fusion-blend alone; this decision only keeps its coin-facing tendencies consistent with that frame and establishes no founding, admission, leadership, or settlement-relations fact.

Sphere, coin class, tally, obligation, hoard, hillfort, and every other label are author-facing qualitative descriptions fixing no in-world name, denomination, metal, unit, price, rate, institution, law, script, or performance guarantee, and no new System mechanic, CAL0 change, project-default adoption, protagonist fact, or development of the parked species or returning peoples is created.
residual_unknowns: Whether the outlet settlement ever tests, re-melts, or strikes metal or coin, and what capability that would actually take, remains open.
The compact's actual finances — how communal burdens are assessed, discharged, and recorded — remain WLD-CULTURE-002's open space.
Harvest-good exchange of every kind, and whether any harvest share ever touches either sphere, remains open under WLD-ECOLOGY-006's standing boundary.
Coin legends, scripts, readability, and all words for money and worth remain the language landscape record's space and then protected unknowns.

Which households hoard, which salvage grounds still yield dispersed coin finds, whether any intact hoard survives on remnant ground under WLD-LOCATION-004's no-cache default, and the accuracy of folk beliefs about the shrinking stock remain open.
The outlet settlement's internal money customs beyond its qualitative coin-sphere tendency remain undeveloped.
Whether returning peoples or other neighbors recognise, want, or refuse imperial coin remains open through neighbor channels only, with no contact fact.
How rites, dowries, or compensation customs interface with either sphere, if at all, remains open.
reopening_conditions: Later accepted work requires a single-sphere economy, or a functioning mint, treasury, assay, or market institution.
The compact's accepted finances cannot be reconciled with coin as the customary medium of movable burden discharge.
The outlet settlement's accepted development makes a region-wide no-mint, no-treasury negative unsupportable.
Later accepted salvage, history, or neighbor work cannot support a thinning, unvalidated, contestable coin stock.
The Author explicitly chooses another exchange pattern.
